text.title: Verb-Object Tool Naming with Namespace Prefix Core Rules
text.summary: The concrete rule for tool names: verb_object form, lowercase snake_case, prefixed by service namespace whenever multiple servers expose similar verbs. 6 testable rules grounding the verb-object-tool-naming methodology. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale.

section.title: Background
section.p: Tool names are part of the prompt. The model selects by name first, description second. A vague or ambiguous name forces the model to read every description on every turn, which collapses selection accuracy as the catalog grows.

One-line form of the first two rules: Every tool name MUST be lowercase snake_case in the form `verb_object` (e.g., `create_issue`, `search_files`). When the agent sees tools from more than one service or MCP server, prepend a service namespace (`github_create_issue`, `stripe_refund_charge`). Anthropic's internal evals show prefix and naming schemes meaningfully change selection accuracy; verb_object mirrors CRUD endpoint conventions Claude saw millions of times in pre-training, while namespaces eliminate name collisions inside MCP aggregators.

rule.statement: Every tool name MUST be lowercase snake_case in the form `verb_object` (e.g. `create_issue`, `search_files`, `apply_patch`). Names of 1 token are forbidden.
rule.rationale: Anthropic internal evals show small renames produce outsized swings; verb_object mirrors CRUD endpoint conventions seen millions of times in pre-training.

rule.statement: When the agent sees tools from more than one service or MCP server, every tool name MUST be prefixed with a service namespace (`github_create_issue`, `stripe_refund_charge`).
rule.rationale: Namespacing eliminates name collisions inside MCP aggregators where multiple servers register `search` or `list`.

rule.statement: Tool names MUST NOT exceed 6 tokens or include marketing nouns (`acme_corp_internal_v2_search_documents_advanced`).
rule.rationale: Long names consume prompt budget and increase lexical-similarity noise across tool pairs.

rule.statement: Renames MUST be data-driven: run eval baseline → rename → rerun eval. Keep the rename only if tool-selection error rate drops measurably.
rule.rationale: Cargo-cult renames degrade catalogs as easily as they fix them; the eval is the source of truth.

rule.statement: Tool name MUST be consistent with `input_schema` arguments and `output_schema` shape: a tool named `search_*` returns a list, `get_*` returns a single record, `*_id` arguments correspond to the entity in the noun.
rule.rationale: Cross-tool consistency lets the model generalize argument-fill across the catalog.

rule.statement: A tool name MUST carry exactly one verb; tools that select the verb through an `action` enum argument (`manage_files(action="copy"|"move"|"delete", ...)`) MUST be split into one atomic tool per verb (`copy_file`, `move_file`, `delete_file`). Audit verdict for such a tool is `split`, not `rename`.
rule.rationale: Polymorphic verb tools push the verb choice out of the name and into the description, so the model must read and remember per-action kwargs; atomic verbs are self-describing and give the runtime a typed schema per tool to validate.
